text: Pose tracking is an important problem that requires identifying unique human pose-instances and matching them temporally across different frames of a video. However, existing pose tracking methods are unable to accurately model temporal relationships and require significant computation, often computing the tracks offline. We present an efficient Multi-person Pose Tracking method, KeyTrack, that only relies on keypoint information without using any RGB or optical flow information to track human keypoints in real-time. Keypoints are tracked using our Pose Entailment method, in which, first, a pair of pose estimates is sampled from different frames in a video and tokenized. Then, a Transformer-based network makes a binary classification as to whether one pose temporally follows another. Furthermore, we improve our top-down pose estimation method with a novel, parameter-free, keypoint refinement technique that improves the keypoint estimates used during the Pose Entailment step. We achieve state-of-the-art results on the PoseTrack'17 and the PoseTrack'18 benchmarks while using only a fraction of the computation required by most other methods for computing the tracking information.

Sáu chó Beagle cái 6 tuần tuổi được tiêm vacxin, sau đó 3 tuần được công cường độc với chủng virus CDV-HUA-04H, đồng thời theo dõi đáp ứng miễn dịch kháng thể bằng phản ứng ELISA. Sau 21 ngày tiêm vacxin lần hai, các chó được công cường độc và kết quả cho thấy lô tiêm vacxin đã tạo ra kháng thể đặc hiệu với virus Carê với hiệu giá trung bình 0,69, lớn hơn giá trị tới hạn. Reinforcement Learning (RL) systems often struggle with out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization, where agents fail to perform effectively in environments that differ significantly from their training data. This paper addresses this critical challenge by proposing a novel representation learning framework designed to enhance OOD generalization in RL. Our approach leverages self-supervised learning techniques to extract robust and transferable features from high-dimensional input spaces, enabling agents to adapt to unseen environments more effectively. We introduce a multi-task training paradigm that encourages the learning of invariant representations, reducing sensitivity to distributional shifts. Experiments conducted on a suite of benchmark environments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing baselines in OOD scenarios, achieving up to a 30% improvement in performance metrics. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the framework, highlighting its ability to disentangle task-relevant features from spurious correlations. The results underscore the potential of our approach to advance the deployment of RL systems in real-world applications, where environmental variability is a common challenge. This work contributes to the growing body of research on robust RL by offering a scalable and practical solution for improving generalization capabilities.  

**Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Out-Of-Distribution Generalization, Representation Learning, Self-Supervised Learning, Multi-Task Learning, Robust AI.

Spectral clustering has emerged as a powerful technique for data partitioning, particularly in scenarios where traditional clustering methods struggle with complex, non-linear structures. This paper presents a novel topological approach to spectral clustering, leveraging concepts from algebraic topology to enhance the robustness and interpretability of clustering results. The proposed method integrates persistent homology, a tool from topological data analysis, to identify and preserve intrinsic geometric features of the data during the clustering process. By constructing a topological representation of the data, our approach improves the quality of the affinity matrix used in spectral clustering, leading to more accurate and stable cluster assignments. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional spectral clustering techniques, particularly in handling noisy and high-dimensional data. The results highlight the potential of topological insights to advance clustering algorithms, offering new avenues for applications in areas such as image segmentation, social network analysis, and bioinformatics. This work contributes to the growing intersection of topology and machine learning, providing a scalable and interpretable framework for spectral clustering.  

**Keywords**: spectral clustering, topological data analysis, persistent homology, affinity matrix, machine learning, data partitioning.

text: In the context of blockchain technology, a **blockchain address** serves as a unique alphanumeric cryptographic identifier for receiving transactions and communications. While not revealing the private key, the public key is utilized for its creation, functioning as the transaction destination for specific users. This address confers a pseudonymous identity, enhancing protection and anonymity [O'Dwyer & Kong, 2021]. Management and access to associated digital assets are exclusively controlled by the recipient's private key. Complementing this, a **cryptocurrency wallet**, whether hardware or software, enables secure storage, management, and interaction with digital assets. Wallets are paramount for user adoption and engagement, improving the overall cryptocurrency experience by offering an intuitive interface [Franco, 2014]. They provide a secure mechanism for safeguarding private keys, which are essential for accessing and managing funds. Through secure private key custody, wallets facilitate sending and receiving transactions, tracking transactional history, and checking account balances. Comprehensive wallet offerings often include features such as address book management, detailed transaction records, and real-time market data, providing a complete suite of tools for managing cryptocurrency holdings.

text: This paper investigates the attention mechanisms in Graph Attention Networks (GATs), a popular deep learning model for graph-structured data. Our objective is to analyze the effectiveness of attention in GATs and identify potential limitations. We employ a systematic approach, combining theoretical analysis and empirical evaluations on benchmark datasets. Our results show that while GATs achieve state-of-the-art performance in many tasks, their attention mechanisms often prioritize node degrees over actual task-relevant information. We also find that the attention weights learned by GATs can be misleading, indicating a need for more interpretable and robust attention mechanisms. Our conclusions highlight the importance of carefully evaluating attention in GATs and propose potential improvements, such as incorporating additional attention supervision or regularization techniques. The key contributions of this research include a deeper understanding of GAT attention mechanisms, novel evaluation metrics, and insights into the development of more effective and interpretable graph neural networks, with implications for applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, and graph-based AI models. text: With the advancements made in deep learning, computer vision problems like object detection and segmentation have seen a great improvement in performance. However, in many real-world applications such as autonomous driving vehicles, the risk associated with incorrect predictions of objects is very high. Standard deep learning models for object detection such as YOLO models are often overconfident in their predictions and do not take into account the uncertainty in predictions on out-of-distribution data. In this work, we propose an efficient and effective approach to model uncertainty in object detection and segmentation tasks using Monte-Carlo DropBlock (MC-DropBlock) based inference. The proposed approach applies drop-block during training time and test time on the convolutional layer of the deep learning models such as YOLO. We show that this leads to a Bayesian convolutional neural network capable of capturing the epistemic uncertainty in the model. Additionally, we capture the aleatoric uncertainty using a Gaussian likelihood. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on modeling uncertainty in object detection and segmentation tasks using out-of-distribution experiments. Experimental results show that MC-DropBlock improves the generalization, calibration, and uncertainty modeling capabilities of YOLO models in object detection and segmentation.

text: –Positional Encoding: Positional encoding is used in transformers to provide positional information, helping the model understand the relative positions of words in the input sequence, as they do not have an inherent notion of word order. This is critical because the self-attention mechanism, while powerful for capturing contextual relationships, processes all tokens simultaneously, effectively losing the sequential information inherent in ordered data. To compensate, positional encodings, often generated using fixed sinusoidal functions (as proposed in the original Transformer architecture) or learned embeddings, are superimposed onto the token embeddings before they are fed into the transformer layers. This augments the token representations with a unique signature indicating their position within the sequence, allowing the model to distinguish between identical tokens appearing at different locations and to capture dependencies that rely on word order. In the specific domain of smart contract vulnerability detection, preserving the precise sequence of operations, function calls, and variable accesses is paramount, as the order of code elements frequently dictates the presence and type of a security flaw. For instance, a reentrancy vulnerability is fundamentally defined by a specific sequence of an external call followed by a state modification, which positional encoding helps the language model recognize and differentiate from benign code patterns, thereby enabling more accurate multi-label classification of complex vulnerabilities like reentrancy, integer overflows, or unchecked external calls.

Furthermore, its architecture supports advanced features like Foreign Data Wrappers (FDW), facilitating seamless integration with external data sources—a common requirement for comprehensive helpdesk solutions needing to pull information from CRM or inventory systems. It provides built-in support for concurrency control, enabling multiple users to access and modify data concurrently; this is achieved through its robust Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) mechanism, which allows simultaneous read and write operations without imposing read locks, ensuring data consistency and high availability by preventing common database contention issues, and guaranteeing that multiple users can access and modify data concurrently without experiencing deadlocks or inconsistent reads, crucial for maintaining the responsiveness and reliability of a high-traffic support system for the Odoo-based helpdesk.

Existing deep reinforcement learning (RL) for session-based recommendations typically necessitates costly online interactions or relies on potentially biased user-behavior models. This work addresses the challenge of learning recommendation policies purely from offline historical interaction logs, without access to real-world data or user models. We propose BCD4Rec: Batch-Constrained Distributional RL for Session-based Recommendations, which leverages advancements in batch (offline) RL and distributional RL to learn from offline logs while accounting for inherently stochastic user rewards due to latent interests. Our results demonstrate that BCD4Rec significantly outperforms behavior policies and strong RL/non-RL baselines in the batch setting, measured by Click Through Rates and Buy Rates. Furthermore, BCD4Rec effectively recommends items from correct latent categories despite large action spaces and mitigates popularity bias prevalent in offline logs, offering a robust offline RL solution.

text: Future wireless networks, driven by the demanding requirements of mobile edge computing (MEC) applications and functions, necessitate the high-capacity and dense deployment of MEC hosts. However, operating such high-capacity MEC hosts significantly increases energy consumption, prompting the exploration of self-powered base station (BS) units. This paper investigates an effective energy dispatch mechanism for self-powered wireless networks with integrated edge computing capabilities. This research first formulates a two-stage linear stochastic programming problem to minimize the total system energy consumption cost while fulfilling energy demand. Subsequently, a semi-distributed data-driven solution, employing a novel multi-agent meta-reinforcement learning (MAMRL) framework, is proposed to address this problem. Within this framework, each BS functions as a local agent, exploring Markovian behavior for energy consumption and generation, and transmitting time-varying features to a meta-agent. The meta-agent then optimizes energy dispatch decisions by incorporating observations from local agents and its own state information, while each BS agent concurrently estimates its energy dispatch policy using parameters learned from the meta-agent. The proposed MAMRL framework is evaluated across deterministic, asymmetric, and stochastic environments, assessing its performance in terms of non-renewable energy usage, energy cost, and prediction accuracy. Experimental results indicate that the MAMRL model significantly reduces non-renewable energy usage by up to 11% and energy costs by 22.4%, achieving 95.8% prediction accuracy when compared against existing baseline methods.

The opioid crisis remains a critical public health challenge, necessitating accurate and timely forecasting of overdose incidents to inform intervention strategies. This paper introduces CASTNet (Community-Attentive Spatio-Temporal Networks), a novel deep learning framework designed to predict opioid overdose trends by leveraging spatio-temporal data with a focus on community-specific dynamics. CASTNet integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial dependencies and temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) to capture temporal patterns, while incorporating an attention mechanism to prioritize community-level features that influence overdose risks. The model is trained and evaluated on a comprehensive dataset comprising overdose incidents, demographic data, and environmental factors across multiple regions. Experimental results demonstrate that CASTNet outperforms existing methods in forecasting accuracy, achieving a 15% improvement in mean absolute error (MAE) compared to state-of-the-art approaches. The framework’s ability to identify high-risk communities and predict overdose trends with high precision highlights its potential for enabling targeted public health interventions. CASTNet represents a significant advancement in spatio-temporal forecasting, offering a scalable and interpretable solution for addressing the opioid crisis and similar public health challenges.  

**Keywords**: opioid overdose forecasting, spatio-temporal networks, graph neural networks, attention mechanisms, public health, deep learning.

As a result, JWTs maintain both the integrity and authenticity of data exchange, contributing significantly to secure information sharing protocols.

text:
Tiny object detection remains a significant challenge in computer vision due to the limited spatial information and low resolution of such objects. This paper investigates the role of the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) in improving detection accuracy for tiny objects by analyzing the effective fusion factor within the FPN architecture. We propose a novel approach to optimize feature fusion by dynamically adjusting the contribution of different pyramid levels based on object scale and contextual information. Our method leverages a lightweight attention mechanism to enhance the fusion process, ensuring that fine-grained details from lower-level features are effectively integrated with semantic-rich higher-level features. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets, including COCO and Pascal VOC, demonstrate that our approach achieves a significant improvement in detection performance for tiny objects, outperforming existing FPN-based methods by 5-7% in mean Average Precision (mAP). The results highlight the importance of adaptive feature fusion in addressing the challenges of tiny object detection. This work contributes to advancing object detection systems, particularly in applications such as surveillance, medical imaging, and autonomous driving, where detecting small objects is critical.  

**Keywords**: Tiny object detection, Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), feature fusion, attention mechanism, computer vision, object detection.

text: In FedAvg, the central server aggregates the model parameters received from participating nodes by averaging them. However, FedAvg suffers from a slower convergence rate and lower accuracy, particularly when dealing with non-IID data distributed across nodes. It is important to note that the contributions of participating nodes to the training process are often unequal, making the uniform averaging of local model parameters potentially suboptimal. To address FedAvg’s convergence limitations, Federated Adaptive Weighting (FedAdp) was proposed. FedAdp mitigates this issue by assigning unique weights to each participating node for updating the global model, based on their contributions in each communication round. These contributions are initially assessed by measuring the angle between the local and global gradient vectors, followed by a non-ar mapping function to quantify the weights. FedAdp demonstrates superior performance over FedAvg, especially with non-IID data. Experimental results reveal that FL training with FedAdp reduces the number of communication rounds required to achieve 95% test accuracy on the MNIST dataset by up to 54.1% compared to FedAvg. Similarly, FedAdp decreases the communication rounds needed to reach 80% test accuracy on the FashionMNIST dataset by up to 45.4% relative to FedAvg. Nevertheless, FedAdp has a limitation: the global gradient may not always align with the expected direction, as some participating nodes may lack data representing all labels, causing local gradients to diverge from the intended path.

text: In this paper we propose a novel image representation called face X-ray for detecting forgery in face images. The face X-ray of an input face image is a greyscale image that reveals whether the input image can be decomposed into the blending of two images from different sources. It does so by showing the blending boundary for a forged image and the absence of blending for a real image. We observe that most existing face manipulation methods share a common step: blending the altered face into an existing background image. For this reason, face X-ray provides an effective way for detecting forgery generated by most existing face manipulation algorithms. Face X-ray is general in the sense that it only assumes the existence of a blending step and does not rely on any knowledge of the artifacts associated with a specific face manipulation technique. Indeed, the algorithm for computing face X-ray can be trained without fake images generated by any of the state-of-the-art face manipulation methods. Extensive experiments show that face X-ray remains effective when applied to forgery generated by unseen face manipulation techniques, while most existing face forgery detection or deepfake detection algorithms experience a significant performance drop.

This paper introduces an unsupervised degradation learning framework for SISR, eliminating the need for paired training data. Our approach leverages a novel degradation model that learns the underlying degradation process directly from unpaired low- and high-resolution images. By combining a generative adversarial network (GAN) with a self-supervised learning mechanism, the proposed method effectively captures complex degradation patterns, such as noise, blur, and compression artifacts. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing unsupervised SISR methods in terms of both visual quality and quantitative metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets. The proposed method also shows robustness to diverse degradation types, making it highly applicable to real-world scenarios. This work advances the field of SISR by providing a practical and scalable solution for unsupervised degradation learning, with potential applications in image restoration and enhancement.

text: Corporate credit rating reflects the level of corporate credit and plays a crucial role in modern financial risk control. But real-world credit rating data usually shows long-tail distributions, which means heavy class imbalanced problem challenging the corporate credit rating system greatly. To tackle that, inspried by the recent advances of pre-train techniques in self-supervised representation learning, we propose a novel framework named Contrastive Pre-training for Corporate Credit Rating (CP4CCR), which utilizes the self-surpervision for getting over class imbalance. Specifically, we propose to, in the first phase, exert constrastive self-superivised pre-training without label information, which want to learn a better class-agnostic initialization. During this phase, two self-supervised task are developed within CP4CCR: (i) Feature Masking (FM) and (ii) Feature Swapping(FS). In the second phase, we can train any standard corporate redit rating model initialized by the pre-trained network. Extensive experiments conducted on the Chinese public-listed corporate rating dataset, prove that CP4CCR can improve the performance of standard corporate credit rating models, especially for class with few samples.

text: In recent years, significant channel morphology changes have been observed in most major rivers in Vietnam, including the Red River, Ma River, and Ca River. This phenomenon has led to considerable challenges in the management and operation of riparian irrigation systems, particularly culverts and pumping stations, during critical water supply periods. text: Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) traditionally presumes unrestricted access to both source and target domain data, with joint training to minimize the domain discrepancy. Nevertheless, such an assumption is often unrealistic in practical applications due to concerns over data privacy and the inefficiency of data transmission. This necessitates the development of methods that optimize network performance in the target domain without recourse to labeled source data. In pursuit of this objective within the context of object detection, this study introduces, for the first time, a source data-free domain adaptive object detection (SFOD) framework by reformulating the challenge as a learning problem with noisy labels. A commonly employed strategy involves leveraging a network pre-trained on the source domain to produce pseudo labels for optimizing the target domain. The principal challenge, however, lies in assessing the quality of these pseudo labels in the absence of ground-truth labels in the target domain. To address this, the paper proposes self-entropy descent (SED) as a metric for identifying a suitable confidence threshold for generating reliable pseudo labels, obviating the need for handcrafted labels. Despite this approach, perfectly clean labels remain unattainable, and comprehensive experimental analysis reveals that false negatives constitute the majority of noise in the generated labels. Targeted mining of false negatives is shown to enhance performance, and this process is facilitated through false negatives simulation via data augmentation, such as Mosaic. Extensive experiments across four representative adaptation tasks substantiate the ability of the proposed framework to readily achieve state-of-the-art performance. Furthermore, these findings prompt a reconsideration within the UDA community regarding the underutilization of labeled source data in current methodologies.

text: Predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of industrial equipment is critical for optimizing maintenance schedules and reducing operational costs. This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating RUL by leveraging time series data and advanced machine learning techniques. We propose a novel approach based on Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) that utilizes time series embeddings to capture temporal dependencies and patterns in sensor data. Our method transforms raw sensor readings into low-dimensional embeddings, enabling efficient feature extraction and improving the model's ability to generalize across diverse datasets. The proposed model is evaluated on publicly available benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. Key findings reveal that our approach achieves a significant reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) when compared to state-of-the-art techniques. The results highlight the potential of RNN-based time series embeddings for real-world applications in predictive maintenance. This research contributes to the field by introducing a scalable and interpretable framework for RUL prediction, which can be adapted to various industrial domains. Keywords: Remaining Useful Life (RUL), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), time series embeddings, predictive maintenance, machine learning.

Scene Graph Generation (SGG) is a critical task in computer vision, aiming to model the relationships between objects in an image as a structured graph. However, existing approaches often treat relation labels as flat categories, overlooking their inherent hierarchical structure, which can lead to suboptimal performance. This paper explores the hierarchical nature of relation labels in SGG and proposes a novel framework to leverage this hierarchy for improved relation prediction. Our approach introduces a hierarchical classification model that captures the dependencies and semantic relationships between different levels of relation labels, from coarse-grained to fine-grained. We evaluate our method on benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in relation prediction accuracy compared to state-of-the-art flat-label approaches. Additionally, our framework enhances interpretability by providing insights into the hierarchical structure of relations. The results highlight the importance of incorporating hierarchical information in SGG and open new avenues for research in structured visual understanding. Key contributions include a scalable hierarchical model, improved performance metrics, and a deeper understanding of relation label semantics. This work has implications for applications such as image captioning, visual question answering, and autonomous systems, where accurate and interpretable scene understanding is crucial.  

**Keywords**: Scene Graph Generation, Hierarchical Classification, Relation Prediction, Computer Vision, Structured Visual Understanding.

This paper addresses the challenge of experience reuse in RL by introducing a novel approach based on Policy Residual Representation (PRR). The objective is to enhance learning efficiency by leveraging past experiences to accelerate policy optimization in new tasks. We propose a framework that encodes the residual differences between policies, enabling the reuse of experiences across tasks with varying dynamics. Our method employs a deep neural network architecture to model these residuals, coupled with a dynamic experience replay mechanism that prioritizes relevant past experiences. Experimental results on benchmark environments demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces the sample complexity and improves convergence rates compared to traditional RL methods. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust performance in transfer learning scenarios, showcasing its ability to generalize across tasks with minimal additional training. The findings highlight the potential of PRR for advancing RL applications in real-world settings, where data efficiency and adaptability are critical. This work contributes a scalable and practical solution for experience reuse, paving the way for more efficient and versatile RL systems.  

**Keywords**: Reinforcement Learning, Experience Reuse, Policy Residual Representation, Transfer Learning, Sample Efficiency, Deep Neural Networks.

text: Property inference attacks aim to reveal statistical properties of a training set, yet are challenging to differentiate from the fundamental objective of statistical machine learning, which is to produce models that capture the underlying properties of a data distribution. Drawing on Yeom et al.'s membership inference framework, we introduce a formal and general definition of property inference attacks that characterizes attacks capable of distinguishing between possible training distributions, thereby generalizing previous approaches that focused on inferring the proportion of specific data types, such as the ratio of females in a dataset. We demonstrate that our definition encompasses existing property inference attacks and also facilitates new attacks, such as those that can uncover the average node degree or clustering coefficient within a training graph. Furthermore, our definition supports a theorem that relates the maximum possible accuracy of inference attacks distinguishing between distributions to the effective size of the dataset leaked by the model. To assess and quantify property inference risks, we perform a series of experiments across diverse distributions using both black-box and white-box attack methodologies. Our findings indicate that inexpensive attacks frequently match the effectiveness of more costly meta-classifier attacks and reveal unexpected asymmetries in attack success rates. Additionally, we extend the current state-of-the-art property inference attack methodology to convolutional neural networks and introduce techniques to identify model parameters that leak the most information, thereby substantially reducing the resource demands of meta-classifier attacks.

text:
Graph representation learning (GRL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for analyzing complex relational data, with applications spanning social networks, biological systems, and recommendation engines. However, the practical deployment of GRL models faces significant challenges that hinder their effectiveness and scalability. This study aims to systematically quantify these challenges, focusing on issues such as data sparsity, scalability to large-scale graphs, and the interpretability of learned representations. We propose a comprehensive evaluation framework that assesses the performance of state-of-the-art GRL algorithms under varying conditions, including graph size, density, and noise levels. Our experiments reveal critical trade-offs between model accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness, highlighting the limitations of existing approaches. Furthermore, we identify key areas for improvement, such as the development of more efficient sampling techniques and the integration of domain-specific knowledge into GRL models. The findings provide actionable insights for researchers and practitioners, offering a roadmap for advancing the field of graph representation learning. This work contributes to the broader understanding of GRL by addressing its practical challenges and proposing directions for future research, ultimately enabling more effective and scalable applications in real-world scenarios.  

**Keywords**: graph representation learning, scalability, interpretability, data sparsity, evaluation framework, relational data.

text: This persistent gap below supervised performance, despite the advancements in self-learning, can be attributed to several inherent challenges within pseudo-labeling methodologies. For instance, the quality of pseudo-labels is often compromised by confirmation bias, where the model reinforces its own errors, particularly for classes that are difficult to distinguish or are underrepresented in the target domain, leading to the propagation of inaccuracies throughout the training process. While techniques such as those employed by DACS attempt to regularize the learning by mixing source and target data at the image or patch level, the primary reliance on softmax cross-entropy for supervising the student model with these pseudo-labels may not sufficiently enforce strong intra-class compactness and inter-class separability in the learned feature space, especially across the domain shift. Similarly, although adversarial training aims for global and class-wise feature alignment, it can sometimes struggle with training stability and may not explicitly optimize for the fine-grained feature consistency required for dense prediction tasks like semantic segmentation. These limitations underscore the need for mechanisms that can learn more discriminative and domain-robust features, perhaps by explicitly contrasting samples at multiple semantic levels to better handle noisy pseudo-labels and improve the model's ability to generalize from the source to the target domain, thereby offering a potential avenue to further enhance adaptation performance and bridge the gap to fully supervised methods.

Our experiments demonstrate that networks fine-tuned with photorealistic cinematically rendered data adapt better and exhibit more robust performance on real medical images compared to non-fine-tuned models. Furthermore, these fine-tuned networks converge optimally with less training data, and diverse rendering conditions enhance model generalizability by preventing patient-specific learning. 4.3.2 Kiến trúc Frontend
Hình 4.13: Kiến trúc Frontend
Hình 4.13 mô tả kiến trúc chi tiết của phần Frontend. Các thành phần chính của kiến trúc frontend được tổ chức trong Đồ án Tốt nghiệp bao gồm: `containers`, `actions`, `reducers`, `store`, và `apps`. `Containers` là các thành phần tổng hợp, chịu trách nhiệm hiển thị giao diện cho ba trang chính: chi tiết lộ trình học, danh sách lộ trình học cần duyệt, và chi tiết duyệt lộ trình học. Mỗi `container` được cấu thành từ nhiều `component` con, tổ chức theo cấu trúc phân cấp dạng cây để tạo nên giao diện hoàn chỉnh của một trang. Ví dụ, `container Path Details` bao gồm hai `component` chính là `LeftSide` và `RightSide`. `Component LeftSide` hiển thị thông tin cơ bản của lộ trình học như tên, mô tả, thumbnail, trạng thái, cùng với hai nút chức năng để thay đổi thông tin cơ bản và nộp lộ trình học. `Component RightSide` hiển thị danh sách các khóa học trong lộ trình đó, kèm theo các nút chức năng như xóa khóa học, thay đổi thứ tự khóa học, xóa lộ trình học, tạo mới khóa học và chọn khóa học từ danh sách. Tương ứng với các tính năng này, `component LeftSide` chứa `component Modal Update Info`, và `component RightSide` chứa các `component` dạng `popup` như `New Course Form`, `Modal Delete`, và `Modal Choose Course` để hiển thị giao diện tương tác và thực thi các chức năng đó. Để dễ dàng truy xuất và tăng tính gọn gàng, dễ hiểu, dễ mở rộng của mã nguồn, các `actions` được đặt tên theo quy ước `đối tượng/hành động`, phân tách bởi dấu `/`. Ví dụ, `action '@@publishPath/OPEN_FILTER'` được sử dụng để lưu trữ thông tin về trạng thái đóng/mở của `popup` cho phép người dùng tùy chỉnh các cài đặt bộ lọc danh sách các lộ trình học đã nộp. Khi một `action` được gọi, nó sẽ kích hoạt các `reducers` tương ứng để thực hiện logic thay đổi trạng thái (state) dựa trên `action` và `payload` được truyền vào. Nếu nghiệp vụ yêu cầu tương tác với `apis` (ví dụ, các lời gọi đến backend), `reducers` sẽ gọi đến `api` tương ứng. Cuối cùng, `reducers` cập nhật trạng thái dựa trên dữ liệu truyền vào cũng như dữ liệu nhận được từ `apis` (nếu có) và chuyển những thay đổi này vào `store` để lưu trữ. Các giao diện trong `containers` sẽ tự động cập nhật ngay khi nhận được thông tin về sự thay đổi trạng thái từ `store`.

text: We study the task of conversational fashion image retrieval via multiturn natural language feedback. Most previous studies are based on single-turn settings. Existing models on multiturn conversational fashion image retrieval have limitations, such as employing traditional models, and leading to ineffective performance. We propose a novel framework that can effectively handle conversational fashion image retrieval with multiturn natural language feedback texts. One characteristic of the framework is that it searches for candidate images based on exploitation of the encoded reference image and feedback text information together with the conversation history. Furthermore, the image fashion attribute information is leveraged via a mutual attention strategy. Since there is no existing fashion dataset suitable for the multiturn setting of our task, we derive a large-scale multiturn fashion dataset via additional manual annotation efforts on an existing single-turn dataset. The experiments show that our proposed model significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

text: In a traditional convolutional layer, the learned filters stay fixed after training. In contrast, we introduce a new framework, the Dynamic Filter Network, where filters are generated dynamically conditioned on an input. We show that this architecture is a powerful one, with increased flexibility thanks to its adaptive nature, yet without an excessive increase in the number of model parameters. A wide variety of filtering operations can be learned this way, including local spatial transformations, but also others like selective (de)blurring or adaptive feature extraction. Moreover, multiple such layers can be combined, e.g. in a recurrent architecture. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the dynamic filter network on the tasks of video and stereo prediction, and reach state-of-the-art performance on the moving MNIST dataset with a much smaller model. By visualizing the learned filters, we illustrate that the network has picked up flow information by only looking at unlabelled training data. This suggests that the network can be used to pretrain networks for various supervised tasks in an unsupervised way, like optical flow and depth estimation.

This paper introduces a novel approach to gradient boosting by incorporating piece-wise linear regression trees (PLRTs) as base learners. Traditional gradient boosting methods often rely on decision trees with constant values in leaf nodes, which can limit their ability to model complex, non-linear relationships. To address this limitation, we propose PLRTs, which utilize linear regression models in each leaf node, enabling more precise approximations of the underlying data patterns. The proposed method combines the strengths of gradient boosting and linear regression, offering improved predictive accuracy and interpretability.  

We evaluate the performance of our approach on several benchmark datasets, comparing it to conventional gradient boosting techniques and other state-of-the-art regression models. Experimental results demonstrate that PLRT-based gradient boosting consistently outperforms traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with intricate data structures. Additionally, we analyze the computational efficiency of the proposed method, showing that it maintains a reasonable trade-off between accuracy and training time.  

The key contribution of this work lies in the integration of piece-wise linear models within the gradient boosting framework, providing a flexible and powerful tool for regression tasks. This approach has significant implications for applications in domains such as finance, healthcare, and predictive analytics, where accurate and interpretable models are critical. Keywords: gradient boosting, piece-wise linear regression, decision trees, machine learning, regression models.

text: Point cloud completion involves deducing the entire geometry of 3D objects from incomplete data. Traditional methods typically rely on a global shape representation derived from the incomplete input to predict the complete point cloud. However, this global representation often leads to the loss of detailed structural information in the local regions of the incomplete point cloud. To tackle this issue, we introduce the Skip-Attention Network (SA-Net) for 3D point cloud completion. Our contributions are twofold. Firstly, we propose a skip-attention mechanism that effectively harnesses local structural details of incomplete point clouds during the inference of missing parts. This mechanism selectively transfers geometric information from local regions of incomplete point clouds to generate complete ones at various resolutions, offering an interpretable view of the completion process. Secondly, to fully leverage the geometric information encoded by the skip-attention mechanism across different resolutions, we present a novel structure-preserving decoder with hierarchical folding for generating complete shapes. This hierarchical folding progressively refines the local regions, maintaining the structure of the complete point cloud generated at higher levels, utilizing the skip-attentioned geometry at corresponding resolutions. Comprehensive experiments on the ShapeNet and KITTI datasets demonstrate that SA-Net surpasses existing state-of-the-art point cloud completion methods.

Trong mô hình này, máy chủ gửi một mã thông báo CSRF dưới dạng một cookie và cùng một mã thông báo đó cũng được nhúng vào một trường ẩn trong biểu mẫu hoặc tiêu đề của yêu cầu. Khi yêu cầu được gửi, JavaScript đọc giá trị cookie và đưa nó vào yêu cầu. Máy chủ sau đó xác minh rằng giá trị trong cookie khớp với giá trị trong yêu cầu. Ưu điểm chính của phương pháp này là tính phi trạng thái ở phía máy chủ, nhưng nó vẫn yêu cầu JavaScript ở phía client để đọc và gửi mã thông báo, và có thể dễ bị tổn thương nếu có lỗ hổng trong cấu hình miền phụ. Ngoài ra, việc sử dụng thuộc tính SameSite cho cookie đã nổi lên như một biện pháp phòng vệ cấp độ trình duyệt quan trọng. Thuộc tính SameSite cho phép máy chủ chỉ định liệu cookie có nên được gửi cùng với các yêu cầu chéo nguồn hay không. Với các giá trị như `Lax`, `Strict`, và `None`, nó cung cấp một lớp bảo vệ mạnh mẽ bằng cách hạn chế việc trình duyệt tự động gửi cookie phiên trong các yêu cầu chéo nguồn. `SameSite=Strict` ngăn chặn việc gửi cookie hoàn toàn trong các yêu cầu chéo nguồn, kể cả khi điều hướng cấp cao nhất, trong khi `SameSite=Lax` cho phép gửi cookie trong một số trường hợp nhất định (ví dụ: điều hướng GET cấp cao nhất). Mặc dù `SameSite` cookies là một biện pháp phòng thủ hiệu quả và dễ triển khai, chúng không phải là giải pháp độc lập hoàn hảo. Chúng có thể không hoạt động trên các trình duyệt cũ không hỗ trợ tính năng này hoặc có thể bị bỏ qua trong một số tình huống cụ thể nếu kẻ tấn công có thể kiểm soát nguồn gốc của yêu cầu. Do đó, việc kết hợp SameSite cookies với các cơ chế bảo vệ dựa trên mã thông báo vẫn là phương pháp tốt nhất. Các framework JavaScript hiện đại như React, Angular và Vue.js thường cung cấp các tiện ích hoặc tích hợp với các thư viện back-end để đơn giản hóa việc triển khai các biện pháp chống CSRF. Ví dụ, Angular có sẵn mô-đun `HttpClient` hỗ trợ tích hợp với cơ chế XSRF token. Tuy nhiên, trách nhiệm cuối cùng vẫn thuộc về nhà phát triển để đảm bảo rằng các biện pháp này được cấu hình đúng cách và được áp dụng xuyên suốt toàn bộ ứng dụng. Việc bỏ qua một điểm cuối API hoặc một biểu mẫu có thể tạo ra một lỗ hổng đáng kể. Một số phương pháp phòng chống khác bao gồm kiểm tra tiêu đề Referer, nhưng phương pháp này không đáng tin cậy do các vấn đề về quyền riêng tư và proxy có thể làm thay đổi hoặc loại bỏ tiêu đề này. Hơn nữa, việc yêu cầu xác nhận của người dùng cho các hành động nhạy cảm cũng có thể giảm thiểu rủi ro CSRF. Tóm lại, việc bảo vệ ứng dụng JavaScript khỏi CSRF đòi hỏi một chiến lược đa tầng, kết hợp các kỹ thuật từ phía máy chủ và phía máy khách, bao gồm mã thông báo xác thực, cấu hình cookie SameSite phù hợp, và việc giáo dục nhà phát triển về các mối đe dọa tiềm ẩn. Mặc dù các framework cung cấp các công cụ hữu ích, việc hiểu rõ các nguyên tắc cơ bản của CSRF và triển khai một cách cẩn thận là chìa khóa để xây dựng các ứng dụng web an toàn và đáng tin cậy trong môi trường ngày càng phức tạp.

This oversight renders current models opaque and untrustworthy, as they can exhibit high confidence on dissimilar test cases and incorrect predictions. We introduce a Bayesian framework for survival models that enhances both the accuracy of survival predictions and the quantification of associated uncertainties. Our methodology integrates variational inference for uncertainty estimation, neural multi-task logistic regression to model nonlinear and time-varying risks, and a sparsity-inducing prior to handle high-dimensional data effectively. This novel combination addresses the deficiencies of traditional models, offering a more transparent and reliable approach to survival analysis.

This paper addresses the challenge of estimating dense scene flow, which captures the 3D motion of objects in a scene, by leveraging stereo disparity and optical flow. The objective is to improve the accuracy and robustness of scene flow estimation, which is critical for applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality. We propose a novel framework that integrates stereo disparity maps and optical flow fields to compute dense scene flow in real-world environments. Our approach combines a deep learning-based disparity estimation model with a state-of-the-art optical flow algorithm, enabling precise alignment of 3D motion vectors across consecutive frames. The proposed method is evaluated on benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing techniques. Key findings reveal that our framework achieves a significant reduction in error rates while maintaining real-time processing capabilities. The results highlight the potential of our approach for applications requiring high-fidelity motion estimation in dynamic scenes. This work contributes to advancing scene flow estimation by providing a scalable and efficient solution that bridges the gap between stereo vision and motion analysis.  

**Keywords**: dense scene flow, stereo disparity, optical flow, 3D motion estimation, deep learning, autonomous systems.

text: 147-word abstract: Motivated by the need for complex modeling of conditional random fields (CRFs) via a Turing complete language and a convenient method for comparing generative-discriminative model pairs, going beyond typical graphical model specifications, this paper proposes a unified approach specifying CRFs generatively using probabilistic logic programs. Our approach involves implementing D-PRISM, a modification of PRISM leveraging its dynamic programming for efficiency, and introducing new CRF models: CRF-BNCs (CRF versions of Bayesian network classifiers) and CRF-LCGs (CRF versions of probabilistic left-corner grammars). Experiments with logistic regression, a linear-chain CRF, and a CRF-CFG empirically confirmed their excellent discriminative performance compared to their generative counterparts, i.e.\ naive Bayes, an HMM and a PCFG; furthermore, the new CRF-BNCs and CRF-LCGs also empirically outperformed their generative counterparts as expected. This work enables future research into more complex CRF architectures and facilitates broader application of the D-PRISM framework for generative-discriminative model comparison and development.

text: Gastrocolic fistula is an uncommon clinical entity characterized by an abnormal communication between the stomach and the colon, with etiologies that can be either benign or malignant. A 54-year-old male patient, diagnosed with colon cancer, was admitted presenting with prolonged diarrhea, fecaloid vomiting, and weight loss. Computed tomography (CT) scan results revealed the presence of a fistulous tract between the stomach and the colon. However, surgical resection of the fistula was not considered an option for this patient. Various medical interventions aimed at mitigating persistent diarrhea proved unsuccessful; octreotide demonstrated some improvement in this case, yet its prohibitive cost limited its sustained use. Malignant gastrocolic fistula typically results from the invasion of a malignant tumor originating from either the stomach or the colon and is associated with a poor prognosis. Nghiên cứu này nhằm mô tả nhu cầu phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ mắt và mũi cũng như các yếu tố liên quan đến 2 loại phẫu thuật này ở Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh (TP HCM). Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện trên bệnh nhân đến Phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ tại Phòng Khám KAT và Bệnh viện Thẩm mỹ Thanh Vân từ tháng 1 năm 2018 đến tháng 6 năm 2019. Phương pháp lấy mẫu thuận tiện với bảng câu hỏi tự thiết kế. Nhập liệu và quản lý số liệu bằng Phần mềm Epidata, phân tích số liệu bằng phần mềm SPSS 14. Kết quả: Mẫu nghiên cứu gồm 1684 đối tượng, nữ chiếm 95,61%. Đa số các bệnh nhân đều trên 18 tuổi và 1/3 bệnh nhân đã từng phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ trước đây. Nhu cầu phẫu thuật mắt và mũi trong nghiên cứu này lần lượt là 80,70% và 22,44%. Cắt da bỏ da thừa vùng mắt, mí tự nhiên và chỉnh hình mũi Sline là những nhu cầu có tỷ lệ cao nhất. Bệnh nhân trên 18 tuổi có nhu cầu phẫu thuật mắt cao hơn, trong khi những người dưới 18 tuổi có nhu cầu phẫu thuật mũi. Nhu cầu phẫu thuật mắt và mũi ở những bệnh nhân có tiền sử phẫu thuật cao hơn những người chưa từng thực hiện, và sự khác biệt này có ý nghĩa thống kê với p < 0,05. Kết luận: Nhu cầu phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ mắt cao hơn mũi. Các yếu tố liên quan đến nhu cầu phẫu thuật gồm có tuổi và tiền sử phẫu thuật thẩm mỹ.

Additionally, the influence of illumination conditions on the perceived color of pH strips was examined, and further experiments were conducted to study the effect of color change on the learning model. text: Incorporating nonlinearity is paramount to predicting the future states of a dynamical system, its response to shocks, and its underlying causal network. However, most existing methods for causality detection and impulse response, such as Vector Autoregression (VAR), assume linearity and are thus unable to capture the complexity. Here, we introduce a vector autoencoder nonlinear autoregression neural network (VANAR) capable of both automatic time series feature extraction for its inputs and functional form estimation. We evaluate VANAR in three ways: first in terms of pure forecast accuracy, second in terms of detecting the correct causality between variables, and lastly in terms of impulse response where we model trajectories given external shocks. These tests were performed on a simulated nonlinear chaotic system and an empirical system using Philippine macroeconomic data. Results show that VANAR significantly outperforms VAR in the forecast and causality tests. VANAR has consistently superior accuracy even over state of the art models such as SARIMA and TBATS. For the impulse response test, both models fail to predict the shocked trajectories of the nonlinear chaotic system. VANAR was robust in its ability to model a wide variety of dynamics, from chaotic, high noise, and low data environments to macroeconomic systems.

Prior empirical analyses indicate that these features can possess pertinent semantic information; consequently, features extracted from models trained on large-scale benchmark datasets (e.g., ImageNet) often demonstrate effective performance on disparate tasks. This work investigates this phenomenon, demonstrating that deep features can be suboptimal as they are acquired through the minimization of empirical risk. The performance of deep features may degrade when the data distribution of the target task diverges from that of the benchmark dataset. Hence, a hierarchically robust optimization method is proposed to learn more generalizable features. Simultaneously considering example-level and concept-level robustness, the problem is formulated as a distributionally robust optimization problem incorporating Wasserstein ambiguity set constraints, for which an efficient algorithm compatible with the conventional training pipeline is proposed. Experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the robust deep representations.

text: Bộ điều phối (Scheduler). Đây là thành phần lập lịch chịu trách nhiệm quản lý các spyder. Nó đảm bảo rằng các spyder không tải quá nhiều các trang web và có thể xử lý lỗi xảy ra trong quá trình thu thập dữ liệu. Để đạt được mục tiêu này, Bộ điều phối thực hiện một loạt các chức năng phức tạp, bao gồm quản lý hàng đợi URL, thực thi chính sách lịch sự (politeness policy) và tối ưu hóa việc sử dụng tài nguyên. Về chính sách lịch sự, Scheduler tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt các quy tắc được định nghĩa trong tệp `robots.txt` của mỗi trang web, đặt ra các khoảng thời gian chờ (crawl delay) giữa các yêu cầu liên tiếp đến cùng một tên miền, đồng thời áp dụng giới hạn tỷ lệ (rate limiting) để ngăn chặn việc gây quá tải cho máy chủ mục tiêu. Điều này không chỉ giúp duy trì mối quan hệ tốt với các quản trị viên web mà còn tránh nguy cơ bị chặn IP hoặc đưa vào danh sách đen do các hành vi thu thập dữ liệu quá hung hãn. Trong trường hợp xảy ra lỗi trong quá trình thu thập dữ liệu, Bộ điều phối đóng vai trò thiết yếu trong việc xác định loại lỗi (ví dụ: lỗi mạng tạm thời, lỗi máy chủ, hoặc lỗi nội dung) và áp dụng các chiến lược phục hồi phù hợp. Các chiến lược này có thể bao gồm việc thử lại yêu cầu sau một khoảng thời gian nhất định với cơ chế lũy thừa gián đoạn (exponential backoff), đánh dấu các URL hoặc tên miền không thể truy cập để tránh truy vấn lại chúng trong tương lai gần, hoặc chuyển hướng các yêu cầu lỗi đến một hàng đợi xử lý riêng để phân tích nguyên nhân sâu hơn. Một chức năng cốt lõi khác của Bộ điều phối là quản lý hàng đợi URL (URL frontier). Hàng đợi này lưu trữ tất cả các URL cần được thu thập, bao gồm cả những URL mới được phát hiện và những URL cần được ghé thăm lại. Scheduler phải sử dụng các thuật toán hiệu quả để duy trì hàng đợi này, ví dụ như sử dụng cấu trúc dữ liệu dựa trên ưu tiên (priority queue) để phân loại các URL dựa trên các tiêu chí như độ sâu của liên kết, mức độ quan trọng của trang, tần suất cập nhật dự kiến, hoặc loại nội dung. Việc loại bỏ các URL trùng lặp (duplicate URLs) là một nhiệm vụ quan trọng khác được thực hiện bởi Bộ điều phối, thường thông qua việc sử dụng hàm băm (hashing) hoặc bộ lọc Bloom (Bloom filter) để đảm bảo tính duy nhất và tránh lãng phí tài nguyên mạng và lưu trữ. Ngoài ra, trong các hệ thống thu thập dữ liệu phân tán quy mô lớn, Bộ điều phối còn chịu trách nhiệm điều phối hoạt động của nhiều thực thể spyder chạy song song. Nó phân bổ các nhiệm vụ thu thập dữ liệu một cách thông minh giữa các spyder, cân bằng tải và giám sát trạng thái hoạt động của chúng. Điều này bao gồm việc theo dõi hiệu suất của từng spyder, phát hiện các spyder bị treo hoặc hoạt động bất thường, và tự động gán lại các nhiệm vụ chưa hoàn thành. Sự hiệu quả của Bộ điều phối ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến tốc độ, phạm vi và độ tin cậy của toàn bộ quá trình thu thập dữ liệu. Nó không chỉ là một cơ chế phòng vệ chống lại việc lạm dụng tài nguyên web mà còn là một bộ não chiến lược, quyết định thứ tự và cách thức khám phá không gian mạng rộng lớn, đảm bảo rằng dữ liệu được thu thập là mới nhất, đầy đủ nhất và có giá trị nhất cho mục đích nghiên cứu hoặc ứng dụng.

Mỗi phương pháp có những ưu và nhược điểm riêng, do đó việc lựa chọn phương pháp phù hợp phụ thuộc vào tình trạng lâm sàng cụ thể và khả năng tiếp cận của bệnh nhân. Applanation tonometry, chẳng hạn, được xem là tiêu chuẩn vàng trong đo nhãn áp nhờ độ chính xác cao, nhưng yêu cầu tiếp xúc trực tiếp với giác mạc và thường cần sử dụng thuốc gây tê. Ngược lại, non-contact tonometry, còn được gọi là "air puff" tonometry, không đòi hỏi tiếp xúc vật lý và do đó giảm nguy cơ lây nhiễm, nhưng có thể kém chính xác hơn trong một số trường hợp. Trong khi đó, rebound tonometry cung cấp một giải pháp trung gian với sự tiện lợi và độ chính xác tương đối, đặc biệt hữu ích trong môi trường lâm sàng di động hoặc với các bệnh nhân trẻ tuổi. Hơn nữa, các nghiên cứu gần đây đã tập trung vào việc phát triển các thiết bị đo nhãn áp liên tục nhằm cung cấp dữ liệu động về biến thiên nhãn áp trong suốt 24 giờ, từ đó cung cấp cái nhìn toàn diện hơn về tình trạng nhãn áp của bệnh nhân. text:
This paper introduces a novel end-to-end framework for super-resolution (SR) from raw image bursts, leveraging the principles of the Lucas-Kanade algorithm to enhance image reconstruction. The objective is to address the limitations of traditional SR methods, which often struggle with noise, motion artifacts, and computational inefficiency when processing burst images. Our approach integrates a deep learning-based pipeline that directly processes raw sensor data, combining optical flow estimation with a multi-frame fusion mechanism to align and merge burst frames effectively. The proposed model employs a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture, optimized for both accuracy and computational efficiency, enabling real-time performance on resource-constrained devices. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM) compared to state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios with complex motion and low-light conditions. The framework also exhibits robustness to varying noise levels and motion blur, making it suitable for practical applications such as mobile photography and medical imaging. This work contributes a scalable and efficient solution for burst-based SR, bridging the gap between classical computer vision techniques and modern deep learning approaches.  

**Keywords**: super-resolution, Lucas-Kanade, raw image bursts, optical flow, deep learning, multi-frame fusion, computational efficiency.

text: This paper addresses the challenge of off-policy evaluation in recommendation systems, where the goal is to estimate the performance of a new policy without deploying it. The objective is to develop a debiased off-policy evaluation method that accurately estimates the expected reward of a target policy using historical data collected from a different behavior policy. We propose a novel approach that combines inverse propensity scoring with a neural network-based estimator to reduce bias and variance in off-policy evaluation. Our method, dubbed Debiased Off-Policy Evaluation (DOPE), uses a multi-task learning framework to learn both the propensity scores and the expected reward simultaneously. Experimental results on real-world datasets demonstrate that DOPE outperforms state-of-the-art off-policy evaluation methods, achieving significant improvements in accuracy and robustness. The key contributions of this research include a debiased off-policy evaluation method, a multi-task learning framework, and a comprehensive evaluation framework for recommendation systems. This work has important implications for the development of more effective and efficient recommendation systems, and can be applied to various domains such as e-commerce, online advertising, and content recommendation. Key keywords: off-policy evaluation, recommendation systems, debiasing, inverse propensity scoring, neural networks, multi-task learning.

This surprisingly simple, theoretically grounded, and practically effective SWF technique facilitates the easy implementation of many traditional linear and nonlinear filters. text: Object detection is a critical component in various visual applications. However, a common challenge lies in the trade-off between detection precision and speed, where fast detectors often suffer from reduced accuracy, particularly when dealing with small objects. To address this limitation, we introduce the Multiple Receptive Field and Small-Object-Focusing Weakly-Supervised Segmentation Network (MRFSWSnet) for achieving rapid object detection. MRFSWSnet incorporates a Multiple Receptive Fields (MRF) block designed to enhance feature discriminability by applying varying weights to different spatial regions of both the object and its surrounding background. Furthermore, to improve the accuracy of small object detection, a specialized weakly-supervised segmentation module, which specifically targets small objects rather than all objects, is integrated into the detection network for auxiliary training. Extensive experiments on the PASCAL VOC and MS COCO detection datasets confirm the efficacy of our method. Notably, using a lower resolution input (300x300), MRFSWSnet achieves an 80.9% mAP on the VOC2007 test set with an impressive inference speed of 15 milliseconds per frame, positioning it as a state-of-the-art real-time detector.

text: A dynamic texture (DT) refers to a sequence of images that exhibit temporal regularities and has many applications in computer vision and graphics. Given an exemplar of dynamic texture, it is a dynamic but challenging task to generate new samples with high quality that are perceptually similar to the input exemplar, which is known to be . Numerous approaches have been devoted to this problem, in the past decades, but none them are able to tackle all kinds of dynamic textures equally well. In this paper, we investigate the synthesizability of dynamic texture samples:  To this end, we propose to learn regression models to connect dynamic texture samples with synthesizability scores, with the help of a compiled dynamic texture dataset annotated in terms of synthesizability. More precisely, we first define the synthesizability of DT samples and characterize them by a set of spatiotemporal features. Based on these features and an annotated dynamic texture dataset, we then train regression models to predict the synthesizability scores of texture samples and learn classifiers to select the most suitable EDTS methods. We further complete the selection, partition and synthesizability prediction of dynamic texture samples in a hierarchical scheme. We finally apply the learned synthesizability to detecting synthesizable regions in videos. The experiments demonstrate that our method can effectively learn and predict the synthesizability of DT samples.

Và trò cụ thể của các package trong mô hình như sau:

**Controller Package** chịu trách nhiệm chính trong việc tiếp nhận các yêu cầu từ phía Frontend, đóng vai trò như cổng vào của hệ thống Backend. Nhiệm vụ của Controller là phân tích yêu cầu HTTP, thực hiện các kiểm tra xác thực và kiểm tra đầu vào cơ bản, sau đó điều phối yêu cầu đến tầng xử lý nghiệp vụ phù hợp. Controller không chứa logic nghiệp vụ phức tạp mà tập trung vào việc định tuyến, chuyển đổi dữ liệu đầu vào và gọi các phương thức tương ứng từ tầng Business. Sau khi tầng Business hoàn tất xử lý và trả về kết quả, Controller sẽ có trách nhiệm định dạng dữ liệu đầu ra (thường là JSON) và gửi phản hồi trở lại cho Frontend. Sự tách biệt này đảm bảo rằng Controller luôn giữ vai trò mỏng (thin controller), giúp code dễ đọc, dễ bảo trì và dễ kiểm thử hơn, đồng thời giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc lẫn nhau giữa các thành phần.

**Business Package (còn được gọi là Service Layer hoặc Logic Layer)** là trái tim của hệ thống Backend, chứa đựng toàn bộ các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và logic xử lý cốt lõi của ứng dụng. Đây là nơi các thao tác phức tạp được thực hiện, ví dụ như tính toán, kiểm tra ràng buộc nghiệp vụ sâu hơn, quản lý các giao dịch phức tạp liên quan đến nhiều thực thể dữ liệu, hoặc tích hợp với các hệ thống bên ngoài. Tầng Business nhận dữ liệu từ Controller, xử lý theo logic đã định, và sau đó tương tác với tầng Model để truy xuất hoặc lưu trữ dữ liệu vào cơ sở dữ liệu. Mọi quyết định về cách thức dữ liệu được xử lý, thay đổi trạng thái, và tương tác giữa các thực thể đều được định nghĩa rõ ràng tại đây. Mục tiêu chính của tầng Business là đảm bảo tính nhất quán, toàn vẹn và đúng đắn của dữ liệu cũng như các quy trình nghiệp vụ. Việc tách biệt logic nghiệp vụ vào một tầng riêng biệt giúp tăng khả năng tái sử dụng code, dễ dàng mở rộng và quan trọng nhất là dễ dàng kiểm thử các quy tắc nghiệp vụ một cách độc lập mà không cần phụ thuộc vào tầng giao diện hay tầng truy cập dữ liệu.

**Model Package** đại diện cho cấu trúc dữ liệu và các thao tác liên quan đến cơ sở dữ liệu. Trong mô hình này, Model thường được chia thành hai phần chính: Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) hoặc Plain Old Java Objects (POJOs)/Plain Old CLR Objects (POCOs) đại diện cho cấu trúc của các thực thể dữ liệu, và Data Access Objects (DAOs) hoặc Repositories chịu trách nhiệm tương tác trực tiếp với cơ sở dữ liệu. Tầng Model cung cấp các phương thức để thực hiện các thao tác CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) dữ liệu, ánh xạ dữ liệu từ cơ sở dữ liệu sang các đối tượng lập trình và ngược lại. Nhiệm vụ của Model là cung cấp một lớp trừu tượng hóa cho việc truy cập dữ liệu, giúp tầng Business không cần phải quan tâm đến chi tiết kỹ thuật của cơ sở dữ liệu (ví dụ: loại cơ sở dữ liệu, câu lệnh SQL cụ thể). Tầng Model không chứa logic nghiệp vụ; nó chỉ tập trung vào việc quản lý và cung cấp dữ liệu một cách hiệu quả và an toàn. Việc tách biệt tầng Model giúp hệ thống dễ dàng thay đổi loại cơ sở dữ liệu hoặc cấu trúc dữ liệu mà không ảnh hưởng đến logic nghiệp vụ, đồng thời cải thiện khả năng bảo trì và kiểm thử của phần mềm.

Sự phân chia rõ ràng các gói Controller, Business và Model trong mô hình Backend này không chỉ giúp tổ chức mã nguồn một cách có hệ thống, mà còn mang lại nhiều lợi ích quan trọng về kiến trúc. Nó thúc đẩy nguyên tắc tách biệt các mối quan tâm (separation of concerns), mỗi package có một vai trò và trách nhiệm cụ thể, độc lập với các package khác. Điều này giúp nâng cao khả năng đọc hiểu mã nguồn, giảm thiểu sự phụ thuộc giữa các module, từ đó cải thiện đáng kể khả năng bảo trì và mở rộng hệ thống. Khi có sự thay đổi về yêu cầu nghiệp vụ, chỉ cần điều chỉnh trong tầng Business; khi giao diện người dùng thay đổi, chỉ cần thay đổi Frontend và Controller; và khi cấu trúc cơ sở dữ liệu thay đổi, chỉ cần cập nhật tầng Model. text: Instance segmentation on 3D point clouds is one of the most extensively researched areas toward the realization of autonomous cars and robots. Certain existing studies have split input point clouds into small regions such as 1m x 1m; one reason for this is that models in the studies cannot consume a large number of points because of the large space complexity. However, because such small regions occasionally include a very small number of instances belonging to the same class, an evaluation using existing metrics such as mAP is largely affected by the category recognition performance. To address these problems, we propose a new method with space complexity O(Np) such that large regions can be consumed, as well as novel metrics for tasks that are independent of the categories or size of the inputs. Our method learns a mapping from input point clouds to an embedding space, where the embeddings form clusters for each instance and distinguish instances using these clusters during testing. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance using both existing and the proposed metrics. Moreover, we show that our new metric can evaluate the performance of a task without being affected by any other condition.
